description: Designing relational databases from requirements to normalised schema, and querying them with the full power of SQL, with a working database server from the second week. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory database systems course.
modelledOn: Elmasri and Navathe, Fundamentals of Database Systems
Silberschatz, Korth and Sudarshan, Database System Concepts
Garcia-Molina, Ullman and Widom, Database Systems: The Complete Book
outcomes: Explain the database approach, the three-schema architecture and the components of a DBMS.
Model a domain as an entity-relationship diagram and map it to relational tables.
Apply functional dependencies to normalise a schema to 3NF and BCNF and judge when to denormalise.
Write SQL queries with filtering, sorting, joins, subqueries, set operators, grouping and window functions.
Create and manage tables, constraints, indexes, views and transactions with DDL and DCL.
Install, configure and administer a database server and connect an application to it.

units.title: Database environment and approaches
topics: File-based systems and their problems; the database approach; data independence
Database users and roles; DBMS functions; advantages and costs
Relational, NoSQL and NewSQL landscape; where each fits
Example domains used all term: a university registry, a clinic, a mobile-money agent network

units.title: System concepts and architecture
topics: Data models, schemas and instances; the three-schema architecture
DBMS languages (DDL, DML, DCL) and interfaces; client-server architecture
Installing and configuring database software: PostgreSQL or MySQL, users, ports, a first database
Tools: psql or mysql CLI, a graphical client, loading sample data

units.title: The relational model
topics: Relations, attributes, tuples, domains; keys: super, candidate, primary, foreign
Integrity constraints: entity, referential, domain; NULL semantics
Relational algebra: select, project, join, union, difference, rename
Relational calculus in brief and how SQL relates to algebra

units.title: Entity-Relationship modelling
topics: Entities, attributes (simple, composite, multivalued, derived), keys
Relationships, cardinality and participation constraints; weak entities
Enhanced ER: specialisation, generalisation, categories; UML class diagrams for data
Mapping ER to relational schemas step by step
Modelling workshop: from interview notes to an ER diagram for a clinic

units.title: Functional dependencies and normalisation
topics: Update, insertion and deletion anomalies; design guidelines
Functional dependencies, Armstrong's axioms, closure, minimal cover
1NF, 2NF, 3NF and BCNF with worked decompositions; lossless join and dependency preservation
Multivalued dependencies and 4NF
When to denormalise for performance and reporting

units.title: SQL: SELECT, restricting and sorting
topics: SELECT, DISTINCT, column aliases, expressions, string and date functions
WHERE with comparison, BETWEEN, IN, LIKE, IS NULL, logical operators
ORDER BY, LIMIT and OFFSET
Aggregates, GROUP BY and HAVING; CASE expressions

units.title: Joins, subqueries and set operators
topics: Inner, left, right and full outer joins; self joins; cross joins; natural joins and USING
Single-row and multi-row subqueries; correlated subqueries; EXISTS and NOT EXISTS
Subqueries in FROM and SELECT; common table expressions; recursive queries for hierarchies
UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT
Window functions: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, running totals
Reading an execution plan and adding an index

units.title: DDL: creating and managing tables
topics: CREATE TABLE with data types, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, NOT NULL, DEFAULT
ALTER TABLE, DROP, TRUNCATE; sequences and auto-increment
INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE; bulk loading from CSV
Views, indexes, schemas; GRANT and REVOKE

units.title: Transactions, storage and administration
topics: ACID properties; COMMIT and ROLLBACK; isolation levels and anomalies
Locks and deadlocks; introduction to recovery and the log
Storage: pages, heap files, B+ tree and hash indexes
Backup, restore, users, roles and basic security configuration

units.title: Databases in applications
topics: Connecting from Python or Java; prepared statements and SQL injection
Stored procedures, functions and triggers
Project: design, normalise, build and query a database for a real local organisation
Preview of NoSQL document and key-value stores

schedule.title: Why databases?
schedule.exercise: Compare a shared spreadsheet and a database for a clinic appointment book, listing three failures of the file approach and how a DBMS addresses each.

tasks.title: Load a flat file of clinic visits, find three redundancy and inconsistency problems in it, and list the queries that expose them
Store the same mobile-money agent records as relational tables and as nested documents, then compare how easily each answers three questions
Draw an architecture diagram for a mobile-money agent network database showing users, applications, the DBMS and storage, and justify the data placement

schedule.title: Data models, architecture and set-up
schedule.exercise: Explain the three-schema architecture with a registry example, showing one change at each level and which levels it affects.

tasks.title: Run one DDL, one DML and one DCL statement on a sample database and classify each statement with the effect it had
Add a column to a base table and show that an existing view still works, demonstrating logical data independence
Create a database with two users of different privileges, load sample data, and check what each user can read, write and create

schedule.title: The relational model and algebra
schedule.exercise: Prove on paper that a natural join can be written as a product, a selection and a projection, and give a small example.

tasks.title: Identify the super, candidate, primary and foreign keys in a five-table registry schema and justify the primary key choice for each table
Write relational algebra for four queries on a student registry, then run the equivalent SQL and check the two results match
Violate entity, referential and domain integrity on purpose in a test schema, record each error, and explain how NULL changes the results of comparisons

schedule.title: Entity-relationship modelling
schedule.exercise: Read interview notes for a pharmacy and produce a list of entities, attributes, keys and relationships with their cardinalities.

tasks.title: Draw an ER diagram with entities, attributes and keys for a school library from a one-paragraph description
Model a clinic with patients, visits and doctors, including participation constraints and a weak entity for prescriptions, and justify each cardinality
Extend a vehicle-registry ER diagram with specialisation of trucks, buses and cars, and decide when to use disjoint or overlapping subclasses

schedule.title: From ER to relational schema
schedule.exercise: Map a given ER diagram to tables by hand following each mapping step in order, writing out the keys and foreign keys.

tasks.title: Map a one-to-many and a many-to-many relationship from an ER diagram to tables with keys and foreign keys, then create them in SQL
Map a weak entity and a specialisation hierarchy to relational tables, create them, and test that the constraints reject bad rows
Turn interview notes from a rural clinic into a complete ER diagram, list your assumptions, and have the diagram checked against five test queries

schedule.title: Anomalies, dependencies and normal forms
schedule.exercise: Find the functional dependencies in a given table of orders, compute attribute closures and decompose to BCNF showing each step.

tasks.title: Show an insertion, a deletion and an update anomaly in a flat table of enrolments by running statements that leave inconsistent data
Compute the closure of an attribute set and a minimal cover for a given set of dependencies, and identify all candidate keys
Decompose a given table to 3NF and then BCNF, prove that the join is lossless, and show which dependency BCNF fails to preserve

schedule.title: Higher normal forms and denormalisation
schedule.exercise: Write a short recommendation on whether to denormalise a reporting table, using query-time numbers and the cost of keeping the copies consistent.

tasks.title: Identify a multivalued dependency in a table of employees, skills and languages, and split it into 4NF tables
Join a normalised four-table sales schema into a reporting table and compare query time for a monthly summary on both designs
Choose which of three redundant columns to denormalise under an update-cost and read-speed constraint, and defend the choice with measurements

schedule.title: Basic SQL queries
schedule.exercise: Write ten queries of rising difficulty for a school database on paper before running them, and mark which results you predicted correctly.

tasks.title: Write SELECT queries with aliases, expressions and string and date functions to list student names and ages from a registry table
Combine comparisons, BETWEEN, IN, LIKE and IS NULL in six queries against a clinic table and explain each unexpected NULL result
Write a grouped report of monthly mobile-money volume by region using HAVING and CASE to flag regions below target, and verify totals by hand

schedule.title: Joins, subqueries and recursion
schedule.exercise: Explain in writing the difference between a correlated subquery and a join for the same question, with the plan each produces.

tasks.title: Join patients to visits with inner and left joins and explain which patients appear in one result but not the other
Answer the same question with a join, an IN subquery and an EXISTS subquery, and confirm that all three return identical rows
Use a recursive common table expression to list every employee under a regional manager with depth, and find the cycle in a faulty hierarchy

schedule.title: Set operators, windows and query plans
schedule.exercise: Write a note describing when a window function is clearer than a self-join, with one example of each.

tasks.title: Use UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT to compare two class registers and list students in both, in one only, and in neither
Rank sales agents within each region with RANK and add a running total of daily collections with a window function
Read the execution plan of a slow query, add the right index, and show the plan and run time before and after

schedule.title: Defining and changing data
schedule.exercise: Write the full CREATE script for a small school fees database with all constraint types and a short test script to prove each constraint works.

tasks.title: Create a table with primary key, foreign key, UNIQUE, CHECK, NOT NULL and DEFAULT constraints, then insert one valid and one invalid row
Bulk load a CSV of 200 rows, then use UPDATE and DELETE with conditions, checking row counts before and after each statement
Create a view that hides salary columns, grant read access on it to a clerk role, and show that the clerk cannot read the base table

schedule.title: Transactions, storage and security
schedule.exercise: Explain with a timeline diagram a lost update and a dirty read, and state the isolation level that prevents each.

tasks.title: Run two transfers inside a transaction, roll one back, and show the account balances before and after each COMMIT or ROLLBACK
Run two interleaved sessions at different isolation levels to reproduce a non-repeatable read and a phantom row, and record what each level allows
Create a deadlock between two transactions, read the lock wait graph, and redesign the access order so the deadlock cannot occur

schedule.title: Applications, procedures and the project
schedule.exercise: Project deliverable: submit a design report with an ER diagram, normalisation steps, the schema script, sample data and ten queries for a real local organisation.

tasks.title: Write a stored function that returns the balance of an account and call it from three queries to check its results
Write a trigger that records every change to a fees table in an audit table, then test it with inserts, updates and deletes
Write a small program that queries a database with prepared statements, then show that string-concatenated input allows SQL injection and the prepared version blocks it
